rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judgment is true because its rewards and punishments match what the books reported through the messengers.
rows.anchor: بأن يطابق الواقع من المثوبات والعقوبات ما وقع الخبر به في الكتب على ألسنة الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No injustice occurs: punishment for an evil deed is not increased beyond its equivalent, and a good deed's reward is not reduced below tenfold.
rows.anchor: فلا يزادون في جزاء السيئة على المثل شيئا ولا ينقصون في جزاء الحسنة عن العشر شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The work for which each soul receives full recompense means good deeds; the word work suits deeds built on knowledge.
rows.anchor: ما عملت } أي من الحسنات , لذلك عبر بالعمل الذي لا يكون إلا مع العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording distinguishes knowledge-based work from all acts, including those driven by desire, while affirming that God knows both.
rows.anchor: مما عمل به بداعية من النفس سواء كان مع مراعاة العلم أو لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by cross-reference: what is stated of work first implies what is stated of acts second, and vice versa.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر ما عملت أولا يدل على ما فعلت ثانيا , وذكر ما يفعلون ثانيا يدل عليه ما يفعلون أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning work best supports the promised just and generous recompense for acts grounded in knowledge; other acts remain known to God though not specified here as recompensed.
rows.anchor: وأما المشتهي فما ذكر أنه يجازي عليه بل الله يعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because warning predominates in this setting, the account of recompense begins with the people subject to divine wrath.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الأغلب على هذه المقامات التحذير , قدم في هذه التوفية حال أهل الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After judgment, the disbelievers are driven swiftly by God's command toward Hell because they veiled their intellect and became confused and astray.
rows.anchor: بأمر يسير من قبلنا بعد إقامة الحساب سوقا عنيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers are described as those who cover the lights of their intellect, leaving matters confused and themselves astray.
rows.anchor: غطوا أنوار عقولهم , فالتبست عليهم الأمور فضلوا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayd glosses the groups as classified kinds, each person gathered with those whose way resembles his.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو عبيد - أصنافا مصنفين , كل شخص مع من يلائمه في الطريقة الزمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is connected to zamr, a confused sound such as the familiar flute, associated with the sound of a crowd.
rows.anchor: مأخوذة من الزمر وهو صوت فيه التباس كالزمر المعروف لأن ذلك الصوت من لازم الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gate shut against its intended entrant signals the disbelievers' humiliation; the gates are opened emphatically once all have arrived, as for assembled criminals in prison.
rows.anchor: إغلاق الباب المقصود عن قاصده دالا على صغاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gates are flung open rapidly after the criminals assemble, releasing Hell's heat and flames to meet them in a state worse than what they chose in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ليخرج إليهم ما كان محبوسا بإغلاقها من الحرارة التي يلقاهم ذكاؤها وشرارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers' question is a scolding rebuke and reproach that compounds the punishment.
rows.anchor: إنكارا عليهم وتقريعا وتوبيخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers from among their own people establish the proof more strongly and make it easier for them to consult the messengers.
rows.anchor: ولما كان قيام الحجة بالمجانس أقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting means continually reminding them; this fits the sura's concern with worship and souls' need for reminders because of their deficiencies.
rows.anchor: يتلون } أي يوالون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God their Lord softens the admonition and makes acceptance more likely, while also recalling the good news available if they had followed.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أمر المحسن أخف على النفس فيكون أدعى إلى القبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warning is more forceful in restraining them, and pointing to this day makes the threatened encounter concrete.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإنذار أبلغ في الزجر قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ellipsis (iḥtibāk) links the mention of the Lord first to omitted majesty second, and the later warning to omitted glad tidings first.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الرب أولا دلالة على حذف الجبروت ثانيا والإنذار ثانيا دليلا على البشارة أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They acknowledge that the messengers came, recited the signs, and warned them.
rows.anchor: أي قد أتونا وتلوا علينا وحذرونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say punishment became due by a decree established in eternity; specifying disbelievers identifies their defining trait as the cause of entry.
rows.anchor: أي وجبت وجوبا يطابقه الواقع , لا يقدر معه على الانفكاك عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive command conveys their utter abasement: they must comply with anyone, great or small, and the gates are Hell's levels.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالمبني للمفعول إشارة ألى أنهم وصلوا إلى أقصى ما يكون من الذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Announcing their eternity as they enter makes the sentence more painful; the wording treats them as fixed to remain there.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإخبار بالخلود حين الدخول أوجع لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant's abode is evil because their pride made the punishment due and led them to its causes; the unqualified wording needs no emphasis after their admission and regret.
rows.anchor: لأنه يقال في الآخرة ولا تكذيب فيها يقتضي التأكيد ولم يتقدم منهم هنا كذب كالنحل بل اعتراف وتندم

none: segment contains only quoted verses and citation markers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to the majestic first-person plural matches the awe and grandeur of the signs shown before the self-exalting king.
rows.anchor: ولفت القول إلى مظر العظمة كما في الآيات التي أظهرها بحضرة هذا الملك المتعاظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs demonstrate God's majesty; the clear authority is an overwhelming command beyond their ability to resist, which kept Pharaoh from harming Moses.
rows.anchor: أمر قاهر عظيم جدا , لا حيلة لهم في مدافعة شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun was a relative of Moses; his eventual opposition shows he was innately set on disbelief despite an earlier profession of faith, and he voiced it in the wilderness without repenting.
rows.anchor: وقارون } أي قريب موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called Moses a magician because they could not overcome him, and a liar because they feared people would believe him; they used sāḥir rather than sāḥḥār to avoid a grammatical misreading as an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: ساحر } لعجزهم عن مقاهرته , ولم يقل , ( سحار ) لئلا يتوهم أحد أنه مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Moses, His specially chosen servant, to Pharaoh, whom the author calls the basest of God's servants, to establish the proof; God bore Pharaoh's denial patiently until every excuse was exhausted.
rows.anchor: فبعث أخص عباده به إلى أخس عباده عنده ليقيم الحجة عليه , وأمهله عندما قابل بالتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses brought the truth, Pharaoh and his followers ordered the sons of those who believed him killed and their women spared, hoping to make the believers deny him.
rows.anchor: قالوا } أي فرعون وأتباعه { اقتلوا } أي قتلا حقيقيا بإزالة الروح

words: وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plot missed both aims: it neither protected them from Moses nor stopped his followers, and instead brought their ruin; tyrants who dig traps for God's allies fall into them.
rows.anchor: بل كان فيه تبارهم وهلاكهم , وكذا أفعال الفجرة مع أولياء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's frightened claim that he could kill Moses if left alone masks his inability to reach him and preempts accusations that he is powerless.
rows.anchor: عندما علم أنه عاجز عن قتله وملاه ما رأى منه خوفا وذعرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh sarcastically tells Moses to call the Lord whose aid he claims is shown by the signs; Pharaoh implies his own gods hold Moses back.
rows.anchor: الذي يدعوه ويدعي إحسانه إليه بما يظهر على يديه من هذه الخوارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh states his fear emphatically because the matter is grave, while some courtiers were minimizing Moses' effect to flatter him and display loyalty.
rows.anchor: مؤكدا إعلاما بأنه الأمر صعب جدا لأنه كان منهم من يوهي أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claims Moses will replace their religion, which the author describes as attributing events to nature rather than worshipping God.
rows.anchor: الذي أنتم عليه من نسبة الفعل إلى الطبيعة بما يدعو إليه من عباده إلهه

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general reading has an open initial vowel and makes corruption appear; the Medinan and Basran readers and Ḥafṣ use the rounded vowel, making Moses the subject who manifests corruption as object.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بفتح حرف المضارعة

rows.speaker: الكوفيون ويعقوب
rows.claim: The Kufans and Yaʿqūb read aw an, presenting Pharaoh's fear as the occurrence of either changing their religion or manifesting what he calls corruption, even if change is not immediate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون ويعقوب ( أو أن ) بمعنى أنه يخاف وقوع أحد الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh calls reform corruption because it opposes his corrupt way, as corrupters characteristically do; he threatens disorder in livelihoods, bloodshed, captivity, and plunder.
rows.anchor: فسمى اللعين الصلاح - لمخالفته لطريقته الفاسدة - فسادا كما هو شأن كل مفسد مع المصلحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' emphatic refuge statement counters Pharaoh and removes the impact of his threats; he declares his refuge at the start of his mission and urges the people to seek refuge too.
rows.anchor: إني عذت } أي اعتصمت عند ابتداء الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By calling God the Lord of both Moses and the audience, Moses appeals to their shared benefactor, who sent him to save them from enemies of religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: ورغبهم في الاعتصام به وثبتهم بقوله : { وربكم } أي المحسن إلينا أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mutakabbir is a tyrannical rebel who exalts himself against the truth, whether Pharaoh or another.
rows.anchor: أي عات طاغ متعظم على الحق هذا وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes one who does not come to believe in the Day of Account.
rows.anchor: لا يتجدد له تصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking refuge means no one can kill Moses because he has sought refuge; the Sender has already secured his rescue and can do anything.
rows.anchor: لأحد منهم إلى قتلي بسبب عوذي , هذا أمر قد فرغ منه مرسلي لخلاصكم , القادر على كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the two leading figures speak, the account turns to a follower's speech, since people without a divinely bound order tend to divide and some speak despite a ruler's control.
rows.anchor: وكانت عادة من لم يكن لهم نظام من الله رابط أن قلوبهم لا تكاد تجتمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man is complete in manhood and firmly believes the message Moses brought.
rows.anchor: أي كامل في رجوليته { مؤمن } أي راسخ الإيمان فيما جاء به موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He belongs to Pharaoh's elite and leading household, a place from which he can advise while remaining among hostile people.
rows.anchor: من آل فرعون } أي وجوههم ورؤسائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He conceals his faith intensely from fear, using indirect counsel to stop them from killing Moses; a lone dissenter from a tribe is more vulnerable than someone among a diverse group.
rows.anchor: يخفيه إخفاءا شديدا خوفا على نفسه لأن الواحد إذا شذ عن قبيلة يطمع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He frames their intended killing as an appalling question and calls Moses a man of great physical and moral stature.
rows.anchor: فقال منكرا له غاية الإنكار : { أتقتلون رجلا } أي هو عظيم في الرجال حسا ومعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He objects that they would kill Moses merely for repeatedly saying his Lord is God, though God has already sent him clear, unambiguous signs.
rows.anchor: لأجل أن { يقول } ولو على سبيل التكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God is Moses' Lord and benefactor, Moses should acknowledge Him; the audience's own dependence on the same Lord should likewise lead them to acknowledge Him.
rows.anchor: وكما أن ربوبيته له اقتضت عنه الاعتراف بها فكذلك ينبغي أن تكون ربوبيته لكم داعية لكم إلى اعترافكم له بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer presents the possibility that Moses is false first because it best dispels suspicion; his lie would harm him alone, not the hearers.
rows.anchor: مقدما القسم الذي هو أنفى للتهمة عنه وأدعى للقبول منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn is deleted from both instances of yakun to compress the warning under extreme pressure: the believer faces three dangers, including exposure of his faith.
rows.anchor: حذف النون فقال : { يك كاذبا فعليه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He still gives the truthful case its due, balancing fairness with the false case and stating that even some threatened consequence is enough to prove the danger.
rows.anchor: إظهارا للنصفة ودفعا للتهمة عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying 'some of what he promises' is measured fairness: acceptance brings all promised good, rejection brings all the threatened evil, but even a part is enough as a warning; the verse uses ellipsis between the two cases.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنهم إن وافوه أصابهم جميع ما وعدهموه من الخير , وإلا دهاهم ما توعدهم من الشر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: An account in al-Ṣaḥīḥ relates that Abu Bakr cited this verse as Quraysh seized the Prophet's clothing during circumambulation; he embraced him in tears until God delivered him, after attackers tore much of his hair.
rows.anchor: كما في الصحيح عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما - أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's description of the transgressor and liar chiefly fits Pharaoh, distancing the speaker from him, though it could also be applied to Moses as Pharaoh alleges.
rows.anchor: بما ينطبق إلى فرعون منفرا منه مع صلاحيته لأرادة موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام على ما زعمه فيه فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An overreacher is one who exceeds bounds by promoting corruption.
rows.anchor: أي بإظهار الفساد متجاوز للحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The liar is persistently excessive in lying; plunging into falsehood is the first sign of being abandoned by guidance.
rows.anchor: لأن أول خذلانه تعمقه في الكذب

words: لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides the moderate and truthful; if Moses lies, his lie harms him and he finds no escape, while if he is truthful, their wrongdoing leaves them unable to find rescue from punishment.
rows.anchor: ويهدي من هو مقتصد صادق , فإن كان كاذبا كما زعمتم ضره كذبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer shifts into counsel that shows he cares for his people, warns them, and grieves for them.
rows.anchor: شرع في وعظهم إظهارا للنصيحة لهم والتحسر عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reminds them that Egypt's present prosperity and dominance over the Israelites and others may turn to affliction, as hardship can give way to ease and ease to hardship.
rows.anchor: غالبين على بني إسرائيل وغيرهم , وما زال أهل البلاء يتوقعون الرخاء , وأهل الرخاء يتوقعون البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dominion is only over Egypt, a land rich in benefits; since they do not own the entire universe, the true God is its sovereign and they should not provoke His anger.
rows.anchor: أي أرض مصر التي هي لحسنها وجمعها المنافع كالأرض كلها

words: فَمَن يَنصُرُنَا مِن بَأْسِ ٱللَّهِ إِن جَآءَنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He includes himself in 'us' after crediting them with power to deflect suspicion and gain a hearing; the conditional treats divine punishment as possible, which a prudent person prepares against.
rows.anchor: أدرج نفسه فيهم عن ذكر الشر بعد إفراده لهم بالملك إبعادا للتهمة وحثا على قبول النصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their own words register that they recognize God as king of kings and lord of lords.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله هذا تسجيل عليهم بأنهم يعرفون أن الله ملك الملوك ورب الأرباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command tells some of God's guards to admit Pharaoh's household and followers to the severest punishment because they followed his misguidance; Pharaoh merits even worse by a fortiori reasoning.
rows.anchor: فالتقدير : نقول لبعض جنودنا : أدخلوا آله لأجل ضلالهم به اليوم

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وحفص
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Yaʿqūb, and Ḥafṣ read the phrase as an imperative meaning 'admit the family of Pharaoh.'
rows.anchor: وجعله نافع وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب وحفص فعل أمر من الإدخال

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومحمد بن كعب
rows.claim: The verse is cited from ʿIkrima and Muḥammad b. Kaʿb as explicit proof of punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: كما نقل عن عكرمة ومحمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic account gives Muhammad knowledge of an ancient hidden event inaccessible except through revelation, and tells him of the future dispute in Hell.
rows.anchor: ولا وصول له إليك إلا من جهتنا , لأنهم يعلمون قطعا أنك ما جالست عالما قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak are the followers, and those who became arrogant are the leaders; both dispute after their worldly relationship fails to help them.
rows.anchor: فيقول الضعفاء } أي الأتباع { للذين استكبروا } أي طلبوا أن يكونوا كبراء

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basran grammarians say tabaʿ may be singular, like jamal, or plural, like khadam (plural of khādim).
rows.anchor: وهو عند البصريين يكون واحدا كجمل ويكون جمعا كخدم جمع خادم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording suggests that the followers obeyed their leaders as one unified body, enabling the leaders' social power.
rows.anchor: ولعله عبر به إشارة إلى أنهم كانوا في عظيم الطواعية لهم على قلب رجل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers ask whether the leaders can protect, compensate, or carry a share of the fire for them.
rows.anchor: أي كافون ومجزون وحاملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrator uses the past tense to affirm the leaders' reply and counter any weak hope that the leaders retain power or pride sufficient to defend them.
rows.anchor: استأنف الخبر عنه بصيغة الماضي تأكيدا لتحقيق وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders say all of them are in the fire, each punished according to what he deserves; no one can reduce another's punishment, and they themselves cannot escape it.
rows.anchor: كل يناله من العذاب بقدر ما يستحقه سواء إن جادلتمونا أو تركتم جدالنا ولا يظلم بك أحدا

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ حَكَمَ بَيْنَ ٱلْعِبَادِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's judgment prevents the worldly practice by which rulers free one criminal and bind another, so the leaders tell the followers to leave them to their punishment.
rows.anchor: حكم الله تعالى مانعا مما كان يفعل في الدنيا من فك المجرم وإيثاق غيره به
